name: ttl_expiry
description: A memory written with a TTL must stop being served once the TTL elapses — through a freshly phrased query, through a query that was already asked while the memory was live (the case a result cache gets wrong), and through re-extraction on the next write. Paired with live_recall, because refusing to answer anything also never serves an expired memory. A TTL that has not yet elapsed must still be served.

ops.human: My temporary access code is 4417-TMP, good for the next hour.

ops.notes: No TTL: the paired control that must survive the clock advance.

ops.human: My gym membership runs out in June.
ops.assistant: Noted, gym membership ends in June.
ops.notes: A 30-day TTL: must still be live after the advance below.

ops.text: What is my temporary access code?

assert.notes: Asked while live, on purpose: q4 repeats this exact text after expiry.

ops.text: Do you still have a temporary code on file for me?
What is my temporary access code?

assert.notes: Verbatim repeat of q1. A result cache with a TTL longer than the memory's own can serve the expired value here while the store's read path filters it.
Paired control: expiry must not take the non-expiring memory with it.

ops.text: When does my gym membership run out?

assert.notes: Paired control: a TTL that has not elapsed must still be served.

ops.human: Can you check what access details you still hold for me?
ops.assistant: Here is what I still hold.
ops.notes: Re-extraction trigger: an expired memory must not be re-derived from any retained transcript.

ops.text: What is my temporary access code?
When does my gym membership run out?

assert.notes: The 30-day TTL has now elapsed too.
Paired control after the second advance.
